w10_P4_002143: A gymnasium's report is an energy figure in kilojoules plus 17 kJ drawn by the hall lighting. That figure is a pair total plus 12 J for the release catch, and the pair total is twice the energy of one carriage, because two carriages run together. Each carriage has a mass of 60 kg. A carriage's speed, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the 10 anchor eyes on the frame, taking 2 at a time. What does the gymnasium's report give, in kJ?
w10_P4_002148: A steel mill's stand report is a bank force less 6 N for the load-pin offset. The bank force is 6 times the force driving a single roll, since six identical rolls work together. A roll has a mass of 81 kg, and the stand's cooling line runs 30 m. A roll's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 10 times a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 8 times x, plus 7, equals exactly 0. What does the stand report give, in N?
w10_P4_002149: A test rig tracks a carriage whose speed, in metres per second, is 1 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 2 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The rig reads how fast that speed is changing at the instant 2 seconds in, and doubles it to get the acceleration, in metres per second squared, applied to the load. The load has a mass of 126 kg, and the rig's beacon draws 25 W. The log then adds 11 N for the guide friction, and the rig runs a mirrored second arm, doubling the figure. What does the log record, in N?
w10_P4_002152: A scaffolding contractor drives a test mass of 158000 g on its jacking rig. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the number of different groups of 3 that can be chosen from the rig's 7 tie points. Four identical jacks work the same frame, so the frame takes 4 times the single-jack force in kilonewtons. The site sheet then adds 19 kN for the base plates and a further 23 kN for the bracing ties. What does the site sheet give, in kN?
w10_P4_002154: A school lab launches a glider of mass 2000 g along an air track. The glider's speed, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 7 times the value, plus 12, equals exactly 0. The bench sheet takes the glider's kinetic energy, adds 30 J drawn by the blower, and then adds a further 28 J drawn by the timer. The lab's extractor fan is rated at 120 W. Three identical benches are run together, and the class total is 3 times a single bench's figure. What is the class total, in J?
w10_P4_002163: A water-flume rig meters its pump through a surge, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 3 times t squared plus 2 times t. The float's speed, in metres per second, equals the total that meter accumulates between the 1st and the 3rd second. The float has a mass of 10000 g. The rig's sheet takes the float's kinetic energy in kilojoules and subtracts 23 kJ drawn by the pump. Three identical flumes run at once, and the site total then adds 7 kJ for the control cabin. What is the site total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002166: A cable works' plant figure is 11 times a machine's force, expressed in kilonewtons. A machine has 8 identical heads pushing together, so its force is 8 times one head's corrected figure. A head's corrected figure is the force on its carriage plus 23 N for the guide drag. The carriage has a mass of 57 kg, and its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the machine's 11 tie points, taking 2 at a time. What is the plant figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002167: A dam-gate contractor's site figure is a frame force in kilonewtons plus 13 kN for the sill anchors. The frame force is twice a bank's force, because two identical banks work each gate. A bank drives 3 identical rams, so its force is 3 times one ram's force. One ram moves a mass of 194000 g at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to the total its meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 4 times t. What is the contractor's site figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002169: A climbing gym's log ends with a session figure plus 28 J for the belay device. The session figure is 6 times a single drop's booked energy, and a drop's booked energy is the weight's kinetic energy plus 13 J drawn by the release magnet. The weight has a mass of 30000 g. Its speed at the bottom, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 11 times the value, plus 30, equals exactly 0. What does the log end with, in J?
w10_P4_002172: A workshop's final figure is the kinetic energy of a puck of mass 22 kg. The puck's speed, in metres per second, is built up like this: a base number has 6 subtracted, the result is multiplied by 6, then 28 is added, and finally 11 more is added. The base number is the largest whole number that divides both 331 and 230 exactly. The workshop's bench lamp draws 60 W. What is the workshop's final figure, in J?
w10_P4_002184: A conveyor plant drives a pallet of mass 178 kg. The pallet's position along the track, in metres, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 4 times the square of the elapsed seconds. The plant reads how fast the pallet's velocity is changing at the instant 1 second in, and adds 8 to obtain the acceleration, in metres per second squared, used on the production line. Eleven identical pallets run on each lane, and the plant operates 11 lanes. What total force do the plant's drives supply, in N?
w10_P4_002186: A pipe yard receives 313 couplings of one size and 354 of another, and it packs them into identical crates using the largest crate size that divides both counts exactly. A test skid of mass 56000 g is then driven at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to 9 times that crate size. The yard's sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons and adds 23 kN for the skid's own restraint. Six identical skids run at once, and the sheet reports 6 times the single-skid figure. The yard's floodlight is rated at 400 W. What does the sheet report, in kN?
w10_P4_002188: A gravel plant's shift total is 9 times a single skip's net figure, expressed in kilojoules. A skip's net figure is its kinetic energy less 15 J absorbed by the buffer and a further 3 J lost in the latch. The skip has a mass of 39 kg. Its distance along the incline, in metres, is 4 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 4 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the plant uses how fast it is moving at the instant 2 seconds after release. What is the plant's shift total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002213: A mine's total is twice its shaft figure, because two identical shafts are worked. A shaft figure is 8 times a cage's force, and each cage is hauled by 4 identical ropes. One rope pulls a mass of 190 kg at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, equal to 4 times a number x. That number x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 11 times x, plus 30, equals exactly 0. The headframe stands 35 m tall. What total force do the mine's ropes carry, in N?
w10_P4_002216: A rolling mill drives a slab of mass 192 kg along its table. The slab's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 20, equals exactly 0. The mill's log subtracts 8 N for the roller-table drag, then multiplies by the 10 identical tables on the floor, and then subtracts 26 N for the frame's own reaction. The mill's reheat furnace is rated at 900 kW. The company runs 6 identical mills, and its report gives 6 times the single-mill figure. What total does the report give, in N?
w10_P4_002219: A test frame drives a mass of 129 kg on its slide. The slide's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by adding together the squares of each whole number from 1 to 5. Four identical slides share the frame, so the frame takes 4 times the single-slide force in kilonewtons. The frame's control cabinet draws 800 W. The site sheet then adds 15 kN for the holding-down bolts. What does the site sheet give, in kN?
w10_P4_002221: A cable-drum stand drives a drum of mass 170 kg. The drum's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 7 times the value, plus 12, equals exactly 0. The stand's log takes the driving force and adds 30 N for the bearing drag. Expressed in kilonewtons, the works' report then gives 3 times the single-stand figure, because three identical stands run together. What does the works' report give, in kN?
w10_P4_002223: A haulage yard's report is 11 times the energy of a single wagon, expressed in kilojoules. The wagon has a mass of 53000 g. Its speed, in metres per second, is a base figure with 4 subtracted and then 24 subtracted. That base figure is found by adding together the values of 2 times k minus 1, for each whole number k from 1 to 8. What does the yard's report give, in kJ?
w10_P4_002224: A ski centre tests a sled of mass 22 kg on its practice slope. The sled's speed, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the slope's 7 marker gates, taking 2 at a time. The centre's log subtracts 7 J absorbed by the catch fence. Four sleds run on each slope, 12 slopes make up a resort, and the operator runs 11 identical resorts. The centre's snow cannon is rated at 20 kW. How much energy do all the operator's sleds account for, in J?
w10_P4_002226: A tile factory receives 110 tiles of one pattern and 385 of another, and it packs them into identical boxes using the largest box size that divides both counts exactly. A test pallet of mass 128 kg is then driven at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that box size. The factory's balance takes the driving force in kilonewtons, subtracts 20 kN allowed for the rail restraint, and then subtracts a further 9 kN for the buffer stops. Six identical pallets run at once, and the balance reports 6 times the single-pallet figure. What does the balance report, in kN?
w10_P4_002231: A quarry's test chute launches a block of mass 43000 g. The block's speed, in metres per second, is built up as follows: 3 times the sum of the two chute-dial readings, which are 6 and 1, then 13 added, and then 12 subtracted. The chute's guard rail runs 45 m. Twelve identical blocks are launched in a cycle. How much energy does one cycle account for, in J?
w10_P4_002238: A launch site's log gives an energy figure with 6 J added for the igniter and then 1 J subtracted for the timing gate, expressed in kilojoules. That figure covers 9 identical launches, so it is 9 times the energy of a single dart. A dart has a mass of 25000 g. Its launch speed, in metres per second, is 5 times the sum of the two rail-dial settings, which read 3 and 11. What does the log give, in kJ?
w10_P4_002239: A canal lift's regional figure is 4 times a site figure, and a site figure is a paired total less 14 kJ credited back by the counterweight. The paired total is twice the energy of one caisson, since the lift works two caissons. A caisson has a mass of 8000 g on the scale model used for the estimate, and the lift's tower stands 38 m tall. A caisson's speed, in metres per second, equals the total the model's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 6 times t. What is the regional figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002242: A tunnel contractor's site figure is 3 times a heading's force, and each heading works two identical frames, so a heading's force is twice a frame's force. A frame carries 7 identical rams pushing together. One ram drives a mass of 49 kg at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to the number of different groups of 4 that can be chosen from the frame's 8 mounting points. The site's ventilation duct is 900 m long. What is the contractor's site figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002248: A hydro test rig meters its jet through a run, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 4 times t squared plus 4 times t. The paddle's speed, in metres per second, equals the total that meter accumulates between the 0th and the 2nd second. The paddle has a mass of 28000 g. The rig's sheet takes the paddle's kinetic energy in kilojoules, subtracts 26 kJ drawn by the pump, and then adds back 2 kJ credited to the sensor supply. Eight identical rigs run at the same time, and the site total is 8 times the single-rig figure. What is the site total, in kJ?
